summary: Identity cookie path namespace collision causes intermittent tenant resolution and cross-tenant auth errors in private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 403/401 errors for admin and service accounts after a recent ingress upgrade. Errors are scoped to a private VPC deployment and only occur for a subset of tenant sessions.

Impact:
- Multiple internal tools for VectorHealth cannot perform tenant-scoped admin actions during the window.
- Errors are intermittent which causes user confusion and increases support load.
- Customer is on a Private deployment with sensitive workflows; they flagged this as impacting a scheduled compliance demo.

Environment:
- Deployment: Private (customer-managed ingress + Redwood private control plane)
- Region: us-west-2 (customer edge)
- Affected services: auth proxy (edge), session-store (redis), control-plane authz checks

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Log into tenant A via SSO (IdP A). Cookie set for domain example.customer-vpc.internal with path "/".
2) Use admin console that opens a hidden iframe making cross-tenant requests to /api/admin scoped to tenant A.
3) After performing a tenant switch to tenant B in another tab, some subsequent requests from the original tab return 403 with an RBAC error for tenant B while UI still shows tenant A.
4) Clearing cookies or opening a fresh incognito session resolves the problem temporarily.

Observed behavior:
- Authorization checks failing because the session cookie presented to the private control plane appears to be associated with the wrong tenant for ~10-30% of requests across affected hosts.
- In logs we see cookie path set to "/app" on some requests and "/" on others; inconsistent cookie-path leads to the ingress proxy routing to the wrong tenant-lookup handler.
- Errors: 401/403 from admin API with message: "RBAC_DENY: tenant mismatch for subject service-account@tenantB".

Expected behavior:
- Session cookies should be namespaced per-tenant or include a tenant-scoped prefix so switching tenants in another tab cannot cause cookie collisions.
- Ingress should honor cookie path + host and not route a tenant A session to tenant B's lookup.

Customer-provided artifacts:
- Redacted cookie dumps (attached in ticket) showing path differences and duplicate cookie names across tenants.
- pcap of requests showing requests that include cookie with path "/app" being routed to a different ingress instance with a different tenant mapping.
- Timeline of recent upgrade: ingress-proxy v2.4.0 rolled 2026-03-08 at 03:00 UTC.

2026-03-12 16:40 - Engineering (comment): Patch branch created: github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-proxy/pull/678. Patch includes: (1) tenant-scoped cookie prefixing, (2) explicit per-tenant cookie path enforcement, (3) feature-flag to opt-in path rewrite in hosted mode only.
investigation_notes: Ingress-proxy v2.4.0 introduced cookie-path-rewrite behavior to support complex hosted routing. For private deployments this caused identical cookie names to be written with inconsistent paths across edge instances.

When a user switches tenant in another tab, the browser may send the cookie variant whose path matches the requested resource. If ingress instances differ in path-rewrite config, the request can be routed to a handler that performs tenant lookups using the wrong header, producing tenant mismatch during RBAC evaluation.
Correlation observed between requests that hit canary ingress nodes (with path-rewrite enabled) and the 403 errors. Non-canary nodes largely returned successful auth checks.
Session-store (redis) held correct session objects; problem is in routing + cookie selection, not session data corruption.
Risk: other private customers with multi-tenant admin consoles using in-tab tenant switches may be impacted if they upgraded ingress-proxy without disabling path rewrite.
Temporary mitigation validated: explicitly set cookie path to tenant-specific prefix and restart ingress instances so they write the same path; this normalized behavior in customer environment.
Next step: ship ingress-proxy patch that disables cookie-path-rewrite for private deployments and implements tenant-scoped cookie naming to prevent collisions.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 - Temporary configuration mitigation applied by VectorHealth under guidance: set cookie_path to /tenant/<tenant-id>/ and recycle ingress pods. Errors dropped to baseline.

2026-03-12 - Engineering created PR #678 which introduces tenant-scoped cookie naming and defaults path-rewrite off for private deployments. Patch also adds a feature-flag that will remain off for private until validated in hosted environments.

Planned rollout: canary deploy patch to staging on 2026-03-15, full private-channel release 2026-03-18 after smoke tests. Customer will be offered automated config update or a manual assist to apply tenant-scoped cookie path if they prefer earlier remediation.

Follow-ups assigned: ENG-2891 (ingress-proxy permanent fix), DOC-142 (update private deployment runbook to include cookie_path hardening), SUP-482560-FU (customer follow-up to confirm post-release behavior).

Postmortem notes to include: clear guidance for private deployments when enabling new proxy features, add automated validation that cookie attributes remain consistent across canary/edge nodes before promoting.
